title: OTP
summary: A public Go library for HOTP and TOTP authentication tokens.
intended_users: Go developers adding interoperable one-time-password verification and provisioning.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Expose standards-based OTP generation and validation through a focused library.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: HOTP counter and TOTP time-window modes address different deployment constraints.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Separate HOTP, TOTP, and provisioning-key responsibilities behind small Go APIs.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Validation-window and secret-handling decisions remain application responsibilities.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Review committed vectors, invalid-input, drift, algorithm, and provisioning tests without executing them.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Revisit boundaries when new standards cannot fit existing algorithm and provisioning interfaces.

testing_strategy: Committed Go tests include standards vectors and boundary cases; Finch never executes them.
security_threat: OTP verification reduces replay of static passwords but secret storage, phishing resistance, endpoint compromise, and application rate limiting remain external risks.
production_limitation: Static evidence does not verify standards conformance, runtime correctness, secure integration, or successful tests.
technical_debt: Integration-specific secret custody and abuse controls require separate review.
track_alignment_explanation: The library directly implements a concrete authentication control.

ai_disclosure.purposes: No upstream AI-use claim; the calibration narrative was prepared without maintainer input.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: Human reference judgment froze before inference.
